clusters.name: User Authentication Strategy
clusters.description: Authentication mechanisms and credential-handling choices that establish user identity, distinct from ongoing session controls and broader data protection.

relations.rationale: Password-based authentication entails protecting credentials during transmission and storage.

values.label: Email/password authentication
values.description: Users authenticate with email and password, with credentials protected during transmission and storage.

clusters.name: Session Lifecycle Control
clusters.description: Policies governing session termination and idle-session behavior after authentication, distinct from the mechanism used to establish identity.

relations.rationale: Session termination policies apply after an authentication mechanism establishes the user session.

values.label: Immediate manual logout
values.description: A user can explicitly sign out, immediately terminating the active session.

values.label: Inactivity-based timeout
values.description: The system automatically terminates sessions after a configured period of inactivity.

clusters.name: Sensitive Data Protection
clusters.description: Safeguards for sensitive information during transmission and persistence, distinct from authentication, storage access, and business processing decisions.

relations.rationale: Encryption and privacy safeguards restrict how repositories and other persistence mechanisms may store sensitive CityBike data.

values.label: End-to-end data encryption
values.description: Sensitive registration and user data are encrypted both in transit and at rest.

clusters.name: Persistence Access Pattern
clusters.description: Patterns for persisting and querying bikes, usage records, and statistics, distinct from the protection applied to stored data.

values.label: Repository-based data access
values.description: Repositories mediate persistence and querying for bike data and usage statistics.

clusters.name: Domain Event Coordination
clusters.description: Cross-component coordination mechanisms for propagating domain changes, distinguished from user-facing notification delivery.

relations.rationale: Domain events and message-based coordination can produce asynchronous updates that feed rider-facing status notifications.

values.label: Asynchronous domain messaging
values.description: Bike lifecycle changes propagate through asynchronous domain events and messages rather than tightly coupled calls.

clusters.name: User Notification Propagation
clusters.description: Mechanisms for delivering user-facing updates about bike status and rental records, distinct from internal event coordination.

values.label: Observer-based status notifications
values.description: An Observer-based mechanism notifies users when bike status or usage-history availability changes.

clusters.name: Rental Pricing Calculation
clusters.description: Architectural variation in calculating rental charges, distinct from notification timing and other platform infrastructure concerns.

values.label: Strategy-based pricing
values.description: A Strategy pattern selects or varies the rental pricing algorithm, while notification timing remains separate.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing taxonomy dimensions. The session-control codes map to Dimension 2 (Session Lifecycle Control), with 'Manual logout terminates session immediately', 'User-initiated sign-out control', 'Inactivity-based session timeout', and 'Forced logout after idle period' all fitting the existing logout/timeout values. 'email/password authentication selected' is covered by Dimension 1 (User Authentication Strategy). The secure transmission, secure storage, and sensitive registration data handling codes are covered by Dimension 3 (Sensitive Data Protection), which already captures encryption/protection of sensitive data in transit and at rest. The observer-based bike status notifications and usage history availability updates are covered by Dimension 6 (User Notification Propagation), while the separate notification timing mechanism is not a new architectural concern relative to the current taxonomy because it is already excluded from the notification-vs-internal coordination split and does not form a distinct axis here. Strategy-based rental pricing calculation is covered by Dimension 7 (Rental Pricing Calculation). Repository-based bike data persistence and usage statistics querying are covered by Dimension 4 (Persistence Access Pattern). The event-driven bike registration workflow, asynchronous domain event handling, and message-based workflow coordination are covered by Dimension 5 (Domain Event Coordination). No open code introduces a clearly distinct, use-case-relevant architectural dimension beyond these existing axes.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing dimensions in the taxonomy. The 30-minute verification-code expiry fits User Authentication Strategy; command-based rental operations fit Application Coordination Pattern; notification scheduling, observer-based rental-state updates, event dispatch/scheduler, pre-expiry notification delivery, and rental-duration tracking are covered by User Notification Propagation; personal data collection, registration security requirements, and optional zip code are covered by Sensitive Data Protection; payment facade/delegation and interchangeable payment methods are covered by Rental Financial Processing Strategy; and real-time bike status monitoring, usage data aggregation, and operational visibility dashboard are covered by Operational Data Access and Monitoring. No open code introduces a distinct architectural concern that would require a new orthogonal dimension for the CityBike use case.
